limitations: Figures were read from secondary summaries; the infographic PDF could not be mapped label-to-number reliably. 387 HNWI respondents. Intentions, not purchases.

label: Betterhomes Dubai transaction split (end user vs investor), as reported by Gulf News
limitations: Market-wide only; sample size not stated; no nationality split.

label: CIA World Factbook, People and Society: Languages (public domain), via the factbook.json mirror; first-language / home-language percentages as published, with the reference year given in each entry
limitations: Census or estimate years differ by country (often 2010-2021). Definitions differ (mother tongue, home language). Many countries publish no percentages.

label: Unicode CLDR supplementalData territoryInfo (language population percent by territory)
limitations: Does not separate first and second language; figures for some territories are old. Used as a language-reach proxy, not a census.

label: Statistics Canada, 2021 Census of Population: language
limitations: Ability to speak versus mother tongue differ; the figure used is ability to speak.

label: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Census 2021: language used at home
limitations: Counts language used at home only.

label: Office for National Statistics, Census 2021 England and Wales: main language
limitations: Main language only, England and Wales only; undercounts speakers who list English as main language.

label: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2021: language spoken at home
limitations: Survey estimate; the figure was read from a secondary summary, not the table itself.

label: Stats NZ, 2018 Census: languages spoken
limitations: The 2023 census gives 49,656 for Punjabi.

label: Joshua Project / PeopleGroups people-group population estimates
limitations: Mission-research estimates of ethnic groups, not a census. Sources disagree by up to 50%.

label: Singapore Department of Statistics, Census 2010 (ethnic and religious categories)
limitations: Ethnic and religious categories, not language.

label: UAE expatriate nationality shares from public summaries (Indians about 27-35%, Pakistanis about 12-17% of roughly 11 million)
limitations: No census by language. Language shares inside each nationality are assumptions.

label: US Census 2010 language spoken at home
limitations: Old; use the latest ACS table when verified.

label: Cyprus census 2021 language figures (via Wikipedia table)
limitations: Read from a secondary table.

label: US Chinese speakers, advocacy summary of Census data (AAJC) and Census Bureau 2019 report
limitations: All Chinese varieties; Mandarin alone not separated.

label: Annual bilateral migrant stocks by country of birth, 1960-2022 (imputed), Mendeley Data cpt3nh6jct, file migration_imputed_RIKS_dec2021.csv, year 2020
licence_or_access: open research data licence (check the dataset page)
limitations: Foreign-born people only (second generation not counted); values are imputed from census and register data, so they are modelled, not counted. Used for destinations Eurostat does not cover.

label: World Bank indicators behind the investment-motivation estimate: stock market capitalisation (% of GDP), personal remittances received (% of GDP), outward investment, consumer price inflation and exchange-rate change
limitations: Used as proxies for the wish to diversify wealth abroad. A proxy for motive, not evidence that anyone buys Dubai property.

label: Brokerage analyses of Dubai Land Department buyer nationalities, 2024-2025 (Benhams, Dubai Tax and Property, Smart Zones, Hanok International, Alsro and others)
limitations: Shares quoted by brokers (India about 22%, UK about 17%, China about 14%, Saudi Arabia about 11%, Russia about 9%). The Dubai Land Department does not publish exact nationality percentages, so these vary by source and period.

label: World Bank GDP per capita (PPP) used to scale the modelled cost per lead by country wealth
limitations: The modelled CPL is an estimate anchored on the client's regional benchmarks, not a measured cost.

label: Country opportunity scores: six dimensions (Dubai demand, financial capacity, motivations, capital access, reachable audience, acquisition economics) with editable weights and client-sales boosts
limitations: Built from the sources above. Missing data counts as a cautious 40 and lowers the score. A model of potential, not a forecast of sales.

label: IMF Annual Report on Exchange Arrangements and Exchange Restrictions (capital controls by country)
limitations: Capital-access scores for countries with controls, sanctions or currency stress are my judgement from general knowledge, not read from this report.

label: Wealth reports with millionaire and HNWI counts by country (Knight Frank Wealth Report, UBS Global Wealth Report, Henley Private Wealth Migration)
limitations: Financial capacity currently uses GDP per head, purchasing power and affluent-audience estimates. Real millionaire counts would be a better signal.

label: Ethnologue language population estimates by country
limitations: Would give speaker numbers for more languages and countries than CLDR and the census figures used.

limitations: Codes only.
